question: A 24-year-old woman at 6 weeks gestation seeks evaluation at a local walk-in clinic because she has noticed a clear, sticky discharge from her right nipple for the past 1 week. The discharge leaves a pink stain on her bra. She does not have pain in her breasts and denies changes in skin color or nipple shape. The past medical history is significant for a major depressive disorder, for which she takes fluoxetine. The family history is negative for breast, endometrial, and ovarian cancers. The physical examination is unremarkable. There are no palpable masses or tenderness on breast exam and no skin discoloration or ulcers. The breasts are symmetric. The nipple discharge on the right side is a pink secretion that is sticky. There are no secretions on the left. The axillary lymph nodes are normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Clear, sticky discharge from right nipple" -> "Pink stain on bra" -> "Unilateral nipple discharge" -> "Sticky secretion on right side only" -> "No secretions on the left" -> "Normal axillary lymph nodes" -> "Likely benign breast condition" -> 80%

CHAIN: "24-year-old woman at 6 weeks gestation" -> "Clear, sticky discharge from right nipple" -> "Pink stain on bra" -> "No pain in breasts" -> "No skin color changes or nipple shape changes" -> "Unremarkable physical examination" -> "Likely benign breast condition" -> 75%
analysis: The most likely diagnosis in this case is drug-induced nipple discharge, specifically related to the patient's use of fluoxetine. The absence of other concerning symptoms, negative family history of cancers, and the sticky pink secretion are all suggestive of this etiology.
